skill.name: Clue + what I know: infer a feeling from what a character does
skill.why: Writers rarely say how characters feel. They show you, and you work it out.
skill.how: Find what the character does. Add what you know about people. Name the feeling.

beats.say: Writers don't always tell you how a character feels.
So find the clue. What does the character do?
beats.show: Mo **slammed the door** and **kicked his bag** across the room.

beats.say: Now add what you know. When do people slam doors?
When they're angry! Clue plus what I know: Mo is angry.
Last, check that the rest of the text agrees.

weDo.text: Tully stared at the scoreboard. Her team had lost by one point. She pulled her cap down over her eyes. She didn't say a word all the way home.
weDo.hint: What does Tully do? When do people hide their eyes and go quiet?
weDo.success: Disappointed. Her team lost, and she hides her face and goes quiet.

options.reason: Excited people usually talk a lot. Tully didn't say a word.
Nervous is about something still to come. The game is over, and her team lost.

weDo.prompt: Tap the clue that shows Gus is scared.
weDo.hint: What does Gus's body do when something moves?
weDo.success: Shaking knees. People's knees shake when they get a fright.

parts.tap: He was holding a cheese sandwich.
parts.reason: Holding a sandwich doesn't show a feeling.

parts.tap: Gus's knees started to shake.
The cupboard smelled like old socks.
parts.reason: A smell tells you about the cupboard, not about how Gus feels.

creature.name: Hunchlet
creature.blurb: A sugar glider that never says how it feels. Watch what it does, add what you know, and you'll have a hunch.

encounters.frame: A Hunchlet is clinging to the pool fence, watching Ava.
encounters.text: Ava stood behind the starting block. Her legs felt like jelly. She kept checking her goggles, again and again. 'What if I come last?' she whispered. Her best friend waved from the stands. Ava didn't even see her. She was too busy taking deep, shaky breaths. Her race was next. When the whistle blew for the race before hers, Ava jumped so high she nearly fell in.
encounters.prompt: How does Ava feel before her race?
encounters.success: Nervous. Jelly legs, shaky breaths and 'What if I come last?' are what worried people feel and say.

options.reason: Impatient people want things to hurry up. Ava's worry is how she'll go: 'What if I come last?'
Nobody has upset Ava. She's worried about coming last, not cross.

encounters.frame: Gus is showing Zed his latest treasure. The Hunchlet is watching Zed's face.
encounters.prompt: Tap the clue that shows Zed is disgusted.
encounters.success: Screwing up your face and covering your mouth is what people do when something is gross.

parts: Gus held up a glass jar. 'This is my snot collection,' he said. 'It took me three years.'

parts.tap: The jar was green and lumpy.
parts.reason: This tells you about the jar, not how Zed feels.

parts.tap: Zed screwed up his face and clapped a hand over his mouth.
Gus gave the jar a little shake.
parts.reason: This is what Gus did. Look for what Zed did.

parts.tap: Outside, the rain kept falling.
parts.reason: This tells you about the weather, not about Zed.

parts: 'Want to hold it?' asked Gus. Zed did not want to hold it.

encounters.frame: Mo wrote a note about Wren's baby wombat. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Bub the baby wombat was hiding under the couch. Wren put a bowl of fresh grass on the floor. Bub sniffed it. Then he gobbled up every bit. He rolled onto his back and wiggled his short legs in the air. Then he did a bouncy little hop around the room. He even did a second lap. Wren laughed so hard she had to sit down.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word Mo got wrong, then choose a better one.
encounters.success: Happy. Wiggling his legs in the air and hopping laps of the room is what a happy animal does.

parts.tap: gobbled
parts.reason: That's right. The story says Bub gobbled up every bit.

parts.tap: hopped
parts.reason: That's right. Bub did a bouncy hop around the room.

parts.tap: grumpy

options.reason: He was hiding at first, but rolling and hopping laps show he isn't scared now.
A sleepy wombat wouldn't do bouncy laps around the room.

encounters.frame: Mo is telling the crew about his little sister's big day.
encounters.text: Mo's little sister, Pip, played her recorder at assembly. She didn't miss a single note. Everyone clapped and cheered. Pip bowed. Then she bowed again. Then she bowed a third time, until the teacher led her off the stage. She ran straight to Mum with a huge grin. 'Did you hear me?' she said. All the way home, she played the song again. And again. Mum wore earmuffs.
encounters.prompt: How does Pip feel after she plays?
encounters.success: Proud. She bows three times, grins and keeps playing the song. She wants everyone to notice.

options.reason: Embarrassed people want to hide. Pip bows three times and grins.
Relief is a big sigh when it is over. Pip keeps bowing and plays the song all the way home.

encounters.frame: The crew went on the ghost tour. The Hunchlet watched them all.
encounters.text: The crew went on the ghost tour at the old lighthouse. It was very dark inside. A door creaked open by itself. Gus jumped and grabbed Mo's arm. Tully hid behind the guide. Zed yawned and checked the time. Indi sat on a step and started counting the bricks in the wall. Then a cold wind blew out the candle.
encounters.prompt: Match each thing a crew member did to the feeling it shows.
encounters.success: Grabbing and hiding show fear. Yawning and counting bricks show someone wants it to be over.

items.text: Gus grabbed Mo's arm.
items.reason: People grab someone's arm when they get a fright.

items.text: Tully hid behind the guide.
items.reason: Hiding behind someone is what you do when you're scared.

items.text: Zed yawned and checked the time.
items.reason: Yawning and checking the time show you want something to be over.

items.text: Indi counted the bricks in the wall.
items.reason: You count bricks when nothing interesting is happening.

encounters.frame: Tully is waiting for dinner. The Hunchlet is keeping out of her way.
encounters.text: The pizza was forty minutes late. Tully kept looking out the window. She drummed her fingers on the table. 'Where IS it?' she groaned. Every time a car went past, she jumped up. Then she sat down again with a huff. She checked the clock for the tenth time. At last the doorbell rang. It was the wrong pizza: pineapple and anchovy. Tully ate four slices anyway.
encounters.prompt: How does Tully feel while she waits?
encounters.success: Impatient. Drumming fingers, groaning and jumping up at every car show she can't wait any longer.

options.reason: Relaxed people don't drum their fingers or jump up at every car.
Worried people fear something bad. Tully just wants the pizza NOW: drumming, groaning, jumping up.

encounters.frame: Zed is going for a record. The Hunchlet is hiding behind the couch.
encounters.text: Zed had been trying to beat the Lava Run record for three weeks. Tonight he was faster than ever. He leapt over the last lava pit with two seconds to spare. Then his character tripped on a tiny rock, just one step from the finish line. The screen flashed GAME OVER. Zed dropped the controller on the couch and pressed his face into a cushion. He let out a long groan that went on and on. 'A rock!' he said into the cushion. 'A tiny, stupid rock!' Then he sat up, rubbed his eyes and pressed restart without another word. His cat, who had seen this many times before, quietly left the room.
encounters.prompt: How does Zed feel when the screen flashes GAME OVER?
encounters.success: Frustrated. He was so close, and groaning into a cushion about 'a tiny, stupid rock' shows it.

options.reason: He was very close to the record, but proud people don't groan into a cushion.
Relieved people are glad something is over. Zed groans, then starts all over again.

encounters.frame: The crew went snorkelling. A big shadow turned up.
encounters.prompt: Tap the clue that shows Indi is calm.
encounters.success: Floating still and breathing slowly is what calm people do, even when everyone else panics.

parts: The crew was snorkelling over the reef when a huge shadow slid underneath them.

parts.tap: Mo splashed so hard that his mask filled with water.
parts.reason: This shows Mo panicking. Look for what Indi does.

parts.tap: Gus shot back to the boat faster than he had ever swum.
parts.reason: This is Gus racing away. Look for what Indi does.

parts.tap: Indi floated still and breathed slowly through her snorkel.

parts: She watched the shadow glide past. It was a manta ray, wider than a car, flapping like a slow, gentle bird.

parts.tap: The water was warm and very clear.
parts.reason: This is about the water, not about how anyone feels.

parts: When it was gone, Indi swam back to the boat. 'Did you see its little face?' she asked. Gus was still hiding under a towel, and Mo was tipping water out of his mask.

encounters.frame: The art show results are in. The Hunchlet is watching Indi closely.
encounters.text: The art show winner was announced at assembly. It wasn't Indi. It was Harper, a new girl in Year 5, who had painted a glowing sunset over the bay. Harper's painting got a gold ribbon and a photo in the newsletter. Everyone clapped. Indi clapped too, but only with two fingers. 'Anyone can paint a sunset,' she muttered to Zed. Harper's painting was hung in the front office. Indi walked past it three times that day and frowned at it every time. That night, she stayed up late painting her own sunset, only bigger. The next day Harper said hello at lunch. Indi suddenly became very interested in her shoes.
encounters.prompt: How does Indi feel about Harper winning?
encounters.success: Jealous. She wanted to win, so she mutters about Harper's sunset and paints a bigger one.

options.reason: Indi didn't win. Muttering about the winner's painting isn't what a proud person does.
She looks away from Harper at the end, but her frowns and muttering are all about the win.

encounters.frame: Gus is showing off his robot at the science fair.
encounters.text: Gus wheeled his robot, Bolt, onto the stage. He polished its head with his sleeve and grinned at the crowd. 'Bolt can make toast,' he said, puffing out his chest. Bolt beeped. Then it turned and rolled straight into the curtain. The crowd laughed. Gus's cheeks went bright red, and he stared at the floor. Bolt came out wearing the curtain like a cape. The judges looked at each other and scratched their heads. One of them turned his notes upside down, as if that might help. Then Bolt handed the head judge a perfect piece of toast. It was golden brown and perfectly square.
encounters.prompt: Match each action to the feeling it shows.
encounters.success: Grinning and puffing out your chest show pride. Red cheeks show embarrassment. Head-scratching shows confusion.

items.text: Gus polished Bolt's head and grinned at the crowd.
items.reason: Showing off your robot and grinning at the crowd is what proud people do.

items.text: Gus puffed out his chest.
items.reason: People puff out their chests when they're proud.

items.text: Gus's cheeks went red and he stared at the floor.
items.reason: Red cheeks and staring at the floor happen when everyone laughs at you.

items.text: The judges looked at each other and scratched their heads.
items.reason: People scratch their heads when they can't work something out.

items.text: A judge turned his notes upside down.
items.reason: Turning your notes upside down shows you're trying to make sense of things.

encounters.frame: Tully wrote a note about Mo's big moment at assembly. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Mo had practised his joke all week. He had even made cue cards. At assembly, he walked up to the microphone. 'Why did the cow cross the road?' he asked. 'To get to the udder side!' Nobody laughed. A baby in the front row started crying. Somebody coughed. Mo's ears turned pink, then red, then purple. He shuffled backwards and hid behind the curtain for the rest of assembly. At lunch, he kept his hood up and ate his sandwich behind the bins. Tully told him the joke was nearly funny. 'I'm never telling a joke again,' he told her. He told three more jokes before the bell.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word Tully got wrong, then choose a better one.
encounters.success: Purple. Ears going pink, red, then purple are a clue to how embarrassed Mo felt.

parts.tap: white
curtain
parts.reason: That fits. He hid there for the rest of assembly.

parts.tap: embarrassed
parts.reason: That fits a joke that flopped. Check each clue in the note against the story.

options.reason: Pale skin goes with a fright. The story says which colours his ears turned.
Look back at the story. It lists the colours his ears turned, one after another.

encounters.frame: A page from an astronaut's diary has floated down to Hollowgum.
encounters.text: Astronaut diary, Day 1. Today I saw Earth from space for the first time. I floated to the window and just stared. I forgot to eat my lunch. I forgot to blink. My friend Sasha called my name three times before I heard her. The oceans were a deep, glowing blue, and the clouds swirled like milk in tea. I could see a storm flashing over a whole country. My hands were pressed flat against the glass. 'Wow,' I whispered, over and over. I have trained for nine years for this, and every single day was worth it. I took 412 photos. None of them look as good as the real thing.
encounters.prompt: How does the astronaut feel looking at Earth?
encounters.success: Amazed. She stares so hard she forgets to eat and blink, and whispers 'wow' over and over.

options.reason: Her photos aren't as good as the real thing, but she says every day of training was worth it.
She says her training was worth it, but mostly she stares, forgets to eat and whispers over and over.

encounters.frame: Tully is replaying the grand final for the crew, again. The Hunchlet watches Kai.
encounters.text: The grand final had come down to a penalty shootout, and Kai was in goal. He had let in the last two kicks. Now it was the final kick of the match. If Pine Gully scored, they would win the cup, but if Kai saved it, the cup would go to Hollowgum. Kai bounced on his toes and wiped his gloves on his shorts again and again. The striker ran in and kicked low to the left. Kai dived, stretched, and felt the ball slam into his fingertips and bounce away. For a second, nobody moved. Then Kai rolled onto his back in the mud and let out a breath that seemed to go on forever. His shoulders sagged. He laughed a wobbly laugh and covered his face with his gloves. 'I thought I was going to be sick,' he told his teammates when they piled on top of him. 'I really thought I was going to be sick.' Up in the stands, his mum sat down for the first time in an hour.
encounters.prompt: How does Kai feel right after the save?
encounters.success: Relieved. The long breath, sagging shoulders and wobbly laugh show the worry has finally drained out.

options.reason: He was nervous before the kick. After the save, his shoulders sag and he lets out a long breath.
His save just won the cup for Hollowgum. There's nothing to be disappointed about.
He covers his face, but he's laughing and his team piles on to celebrate. Nothing embarrassing happened.

encounters.frame: Wren has been looking after a baby ringtail possum. The Hunchlet is a bit jealous.
encounters.prompt: Tap the clue that shows the possum finally feels safe with Wren.
encounters.success: Animals only fall asleep on you when they feel safe. That's the clue plus what you know.

parts: Wren had been looking after the baby ringtail possum for a week. She had found it alone in a drain after a storm, cold and squeaking. On the first night,

parts.tap: it hissed and curled into a tight ball in the corner of its box.
parts.reason: Hissing and curling up show it was scared on the first night, not safe.

parts: On the second night, Wren held out a slice of apple.

parts.tap: The possum sniffed it, snatched it and scurried back to its corner.
parts.reason: It wanted the apple, but running back to its corner shows it still wasn't sure of Wren.

parts: By the fifth night, it would eat from her hand, but only if she kept perfectly still. Wren talked to it softly every evening, telling it about her day.

parts.tap: Wren sat so still that her foot went to sleep.
parts.reason: This is what Wren did. Look for what the possum does.

parts.tap: The possum climbed up her sleeve, curled up in the crook of her elbow and fell asleep.

parts: Its tail was wrapped around her wrist like a bracelet.

parts.tap: Wren didn't dare move for two hours.
parts.reason: This shows what Wren did, not how the possum feels.

parts: Gus brought her a cup of tea and a pillow, and quietly took a photo for the Field Guide.

encounters.frame: Lila's school concert is in full swing. So is her grandad.
encounters.text: Lila had practised her violin solo for months, and the concert hall was packed. Her whole family had come to watch, and they had promised to behave. Halfway through the second song, she heard a familiar whoop from the back row. It was Grandad. He was standing up and waving a scarf over his head. Then he started dancing in the aisle, doing the move he called 'the shuffling crab'. People turned around to stare. Somebody's phone flashed as they took a photo. Grandad added a spin. Lila felt her cheeks burn. She sank lower and lower in her chair, until her music stand nearly hid her face. When the girl next to her whispered, 'Who is that?', Lila shrugged and said, 'No idea.' She missed two notes in a row and stared hard at her music, wishing the song would end. Afterwards, in the car park, Grandad asked if she'd seen his moves. Lila pulled her hood right down over her face.
encounters.prompt: How does Lila feel while Grandad is dancing?
encounters.success: Embarrassed. Burning cheeks, hiding behind her music stand and pretending not to know him all show it.

options.reason: Proud people show off the person they're proud of. Lila pretends she doesn't know him.
Burning cheeks can mean anger, but she hides and pretends not to know him. She never glares at him.
Excited people join in. Lila sinks down and hides behind her music stand.

encounters.frame: Something is glowing on deck at midnight. The Hunchlet is watching three crew members.
encounters.text: Most of the crew were asleep in their hammocks. At midnight, a glowing white shape floated across the deck of the ship. It had a lumpy shape and seemed to be wearing thongs. Gus saw it first. He dived behind a barrel, covered his eyes and whimpered. Zed didn't run. He crept closer, tilting his head, trying to work out what was making the glow. Tully just sighed loudly and rolled her eyes. 'It's obviously Mo in a sheet,' she said. 'Again.' The shape let out a long, wobbly 'Woooo'. Gus grabbed the torch with both shaking hands and pointed it in completely the wrong direction. Zed reached out and lifted the corner of the sheet to peek underneath. Tully folded her arms and tapped her foot. 'Some of us are trying to sleep, Mo.' Under the sheet, Mo was holding a glow stick and a bag of marshmallows. 'Worth it,' he said. He offered everyone a marshmallow. Nobody took one except Zed.
encounters.prompt: Match each action to the feeling it shows.
encounters.success: Hiding and shaking show terror. Creeping closer shows curiosity. Eye-rolling and foot-tapping show annoyance.

items.text: Gus dived behind a barrel and covered his eyes.
items.reason: Diving for cover and hiding your eyes is what terrified people do.

items.text: Gus grabbed the torch with shaking hands.
items.reason: Shaking hands show Gus is terrified.

items.text: Zed crept closer to work out what was glowing.
items.reason: Moving closer to work something out shows Zed wants to know more.

items.text: Zed lifted the sheet to peek underneath.
items.reason: Peeking underneath shows Zed wants to find out what's there.

items.text: Tully rolled her eyes and sighed loudly.
items.reason: Eye-rolling and loud sighs show Tully is fed up with Mo's trick.

items.text: Tully folded her arms and tapped her foot.
items.reason: Folded arms and a tapping foot show Tully wants this to stop.

encounters.frame: Wren wrote a note about the Great Maggot Mystery. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Gus had been raising a jar of maggots for his science project, and he checked on them every morning before school. They were for an experiment on how fast flies grow. He had named the biggest one Kevin. On Tuesday, he came into the kitchen and found the jar gone from the windowsill. 'Has anyone seen my maggots?' he asked. Mo, who was sitting at the table, suddenly became very busy buttering a piece of toast that was already buttered. He didn't look up. His ears went bright red. 'Maggots? No. What maggots?' he said, much too quickly. Then he offered to wash the dishes, which he had never done before in his life. After that, he offered to clean Gus's room. Later, Gus found a broken jar wrapped in newspaper at the bottom of the bin, and three hundred maggots wriggling happily under the fridge. Mo couldn't look Gus in the eye for the rest of the day.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word Wren got wrong, then choose a better one.
encounters.success: Much too quickly. Rushing to say no is a clue that Mo feels guilty about the maggots.

parts: When Gus asked about the maggots, Mo answered

parts.tap: slowly
look up
parts.reason: That fits. The story says he didn't look up.

parts.tap: guilty
parts.reason: That fits Mo hiding what he did. Check each clue in the note against the story.

options.reason: Nothing says Mo whispered. Find the words that tell you how he answered.
Mo doesn't laugh. Find the words that tell you how he answered Gus.
The story tells you how fast Mo answered, not how polite he was.

encounters.frame: It's the first night of school camp. The Hunchlet has stowed away in Sami's bag.
encounters.text: On the first night of school camp, Sami sat at the end of the long table with her spaghetti. The dining hall was loud and smelled of tomato sauce. Everyone else was laughing and slurping. Sami twirled one strand around her fork, then put it down. 'Nonna makes it with real basil,' she said quietly, to nobody in particular. She took a small photo out of her pocket and looked at it for a long time. It was her family on their back step, all squinting into the sun. After dinner, while the others played spotlight, Sami sat on her bunk, the one nearest the door, and counted the days on her fingers. Four more sleeps. She went to bed early, holding her nonna's old tea towel, which still smelled a little like garlic. In the morning, the camp leader asked if she was okay. Sami said she was fine, then asked how far it was to the phone.
encounters.prompt: How does Sami feel on the first night of camp?
encounters.success: Homesick. The family photo, Nonna's tea towel and counting the sleeps all point back home.

options.reason: Nothing says she's ill. She looks at a family photo and counts the days until home.
Everyone else laughs and plays, but Sami sits alone and goes to bed early.
She does keep to herself, but look at what she thinks about: Nonna, the photo, the sleeps left.

encounters.frame: Nia has written up her first dive for the Hollowgum Reef newsletter.
encounters.text: Nia had been dreading this dive for weeks. Her big brother had spent the whole boat ride telling her that whale sharks were the biggest fish in the ocean, as long as a bus, with mouths wide enough to swallow a wheelie bin. By the time the skipper called 'Fins on!', her hands were trembling so badly that he had to do up her mask strap for her. She slipped into the water last, clinging to the ladder. Then the shark arrived. It rose out of the blue haze below her like a spotted island, slow and enormous, its mouth gaping open as it sieved the water for tiny shrimp. Nia let go of the ladder. She forgot to kick. She forgot to check where her brother was. She simply hung there in the water, eyes wide behind her mask, as the shark glided past close enough to count the white spots on its back. When it had gone, she surfaced, spat out her snorkel and stared at the place where it had disappeared. For once, she didn't say a word. Back on the boat, she sat wrapped in a towel, still gazing at the water, and quietly asked the skipper if they could come back tomorrow.
encounters.prompt: How does Nia feel as the shark glides past?
encounters.success: Amazed. She lets go of the ladder, forgets everything else and stares. Then she wants to come back.

options.reason: She was terrified before. When the shark appears, she lets go of the ladder, and later asks to come back.
She asks to come back tomorrow. People don't do that after a disappointing dive.
Impatient people want things to hurry up. Nia hangs still and watches until it's gone.

encounters.frame: The Island Robotics Challenge results are in. Gus says he's fine. The Hunchlet isn't so sure.
encounters.prompt: Gus says he's fine. Tap the action that shows he's more upset than he says.
encounters.success: Leaving without looking at anyone shows the hurt he's hiding. His words say fine, but his actions don't.

parts: The judges announced the results of the Island Robotics Challenge in reverse order. Gus's robot, Clank, had been the favourite all week, and Gus had barely slept for a month getting it ready. He had even made Clank a tiny bow tie for the judging. When third place was called and it wasn't Clank, Gus smiled. When second place went to another team, he kept smiling. Then the winner was announced, and it was a robot called Duster, which mostly just swept the floor in neat little circles. Some people in the crowd gasped. The judges said Duster's design was simple, clever and very reliable.

parts.tap: Gus walked straight over and shook hands with Duster's builder.
parts.reason: Shaking hands is being a good sport. It doesn't show how upset he is.

parts.tap: Then he asked her how Duster's sensors worked.
parts.reason: Asking about Duster's sensors is being curious and polite. It doesn't show he's hurt.

parts: When Tully asked if he was okay, he said, 'Totally fine. Honestly. It's just a competition.'

parts.tap: The other teams cheered and crowded around Duster for photos.
parts.reason: This is what the other teams did. Look for what Gus does.

parts.tap: Gus packed Clank into its box without looking at anyone and slipped out before the photos.
Duster's builder held the trophy high above her head.
parts.reason: This is the winner celebrating. It tells you nothing about Gus.

parts: Tully gave Mo a worried look. The crew didn't see Gus again until dinner, when he said he wasn't hungry, which had never happened before. Even Mo's famous sausage rolls stayed on the plate.

encounters.frame: Zed made the final of the Hollowgum Kart Cup. The Hunchlet watched both players.
encounters.text: The final of the Hollowgum Kart Cup came down to three laps between Zed and a Year 6 boy called Rex, who had won the cup two years running. About fifty kids had squeezed into the library to watch on the big screen. Before the race, Zed kept wiping his palms on his shorts and checking his controller's battery, even though he had charged it twice. Rex, meanwhile, leaned back in his chair with his hands behind his head and told the crowd he would 'try not to lap anyone'. On lap one, Rex skidded on a banana skin and slid off the track. He slammed his fist on the table and growled at the screen through gritted teeth. On lap two, Zed's hands were shaking so much that he clipped a wall, and he whispered 'come on, come on' under his breath the whole way round. Rex caught up and overtook him with a smirk, glancing back as he went past. On the final straight, Zed hit a boost pad and crossed the line a tenth of a second ahead. The crowd went wild. Zed let out an enormous breath, slumped back in his chair and closed his eyes. Rex stared at the scoreboard for a long moment, then threw his cap on the floor.
encounters.prompt: Match each action to the feeling it shows best.
encounters.success: You matched actions to feelings, not who won or lost. Each action had its own clue.

items.text: Zed kept wiping his palms and checking a battery he had charged twice.
items.reason: Sweaty palms and re-checking something that's already fine are both signs of nerves.

items.text: Rex leaned back with his hands behind his head.
items.reason: Leaning back like that, and joking about lapping people, shows Rex thinks he's already won.

items.text: Rex slammed his fist on the table and growled at the screen.
items.reason: Slamming and growling after skidding off the track shows Rex is frustrated.

items.text: Zed's hands shook so much that he clipped a wall.
items.reason: Hands that shake so badly you crash are a sign of nerves.

items.text: Rex overtook Zed with a smirk and glanced back.
items.reason: A smirk and a look back show Rex is pleased with himself.

items.text: Zed let out an enormous breath and slumped back.
items.reason: A huge breath out and slumping back show the worry is finally over.

items.text: Rex stared at the scoreboard, then threw his cap on the floor.
items.reason: Throwing his cap after losing shows Rex is frustrated.

encounters.frame: The Hunchlet found Nell's story tucked inside the old lighthouse door.
encounters.text: Nell had only meant to look around the old lighthouse, not take anything. It had been empty for forty years, and the door creaked like an old ship. But when she found the tarnished brass key hanging on a nail beside the keeper's empty bed, she slipped it into her pocket before she could think. That night, back home, she put it in her sock drawer. Then she took it out and put it under her mattress. Then she moved it to a shoebox at the back of the wardrobe, as far from her bed as it could possibly go. She couldn't stop picturing the empty nail. Every time the wind rattled the window, she glanced at the wardrobe. At dinner, when Dad mentioned that the lighthouse was being turned into a museum, Nell knocked over her glass of water. 'Have you been up there?' he asked. 'No,' she said, and immediately felt her face go hot. She lay awake until two in the morning, staring at the wardrobe door. The next afternoon, she rode her bike all the way back to the lighthouse, hung the key back on its nail, and left a note underneath that said, in very small writing, 'Sorry. I won't do it again.' On the ride home, she sang the whole way.

encounters.frame: Zed wrote a note about Ms Rao's farewell for the school newsletter. One word is wrong.
encounters.text: Ms Rao had taught art at Hollowgum Primary for thirty-one years, and Friday was her last day. She had once let the whole class paint the staffroom ceiling with stars. Indi had spent three weeks secretly painting her portrait, working in the library at lunchtime so that Ms Rao wouldn't see. In the painting, Ms Rao was wearing her famous paint-splattered apron, with a pencil tucked behind each ear, surrounded by tiny drawings of every mural the school had painted with her. At the farewell assembly, Indi carried it up onto the stage, so nervous she nearly dropped it on the stairs, and pulled off the sheet. The hall went quiet. For a moment, Ms Rao didn't say anything at all. She put a hand over her heart. Her chin wobbled, and she blinked hard several times. Then she took off her glasses and wiped her eyes with the corner of her sleeve. 'Nobody has ever painted me before,' she said, in a voice that came out much smaller than usual. She hugged Indi for so long that the principal started the next item without them. The portrait now hangs in Ms Rao's hallway at home, and she sends Indi a photo of it every year on the last day of term.

encounters.frame: Someone has eaten half of Tully's cake. The Hunchlet is watching Tully investigate.
encounters.text: When Tully came home from footy training, the chocolate cake on the kitchen bench had a large, cake-shaped gap in it. It was her birthday cake, and she had been saving the biggest piece for after training. Mo was on the couch, reading a cookbook upside down. There was a smear of chocolate on its cover, and another on his chin. 'Big day?' Tully asked. 'Very quiet,' said Mo. 'I've been reading.' Tully narrowed her eyes. She walked slowly around the bench, counting the slices that were left. Then she lifted the lid of the bin and peered inside, where a single chocolate-smeared fork was lying on top. She looked at the fork. She looked at Mo. She leaned in close and sniffed. 'Why does your breath smell like chocolate?' 'Toothpaste,' said Mo. 'Chocolate toothpaste. It's new.' Tully raised one eyebrow and said nothing for a very long time. Then she checked the couch cushions, where she found a trail of crumbs leading straight to Mo's left pocket. 'That's where I keep my emergency crumbs,' Mo explained. Tully took a photo of the crumbs, a photo of the fork and a photo of Mo's face, and sent all three to the crew chat with the caption 'EVIDENCE'. Outside, a magpie watched through the window as if it knew something.
